newsitem.title: USA: Clinton declares disaster in California, Massachusetts.
newsitem.headline: Clinton declares disaster in California, Massachusetts.

text.p: President Clinton Wednesday declared portions of California a disaster area because of wind-driven wildfires and made federal aid available for flood victims in Massachusetts.
"Due to the devastating effects of the Southern California fires, I am declaring that a major emergency exists in the state," Clinton said in a statement issued by the White House.
"As a result, federal funds will begin to flow immediately to the people and communities ... affected by this tragedy," Clinton said.
The action makes federal aid available to Los Angeles, Orange and San Diego counties, where firefighters have been battling major blazes that have consumed more than 13,000 acres (5,300 hectares).
The declaration for Massachusetts was issued to deal with recovery efforts in five counties struck by extreme storms and flooding earlier this week.
In a statement, Clinton assured the people of Massachusetts that "we will do everything we can to see that you receive all the assistance you need to restore your communities."
Federal funds will be available for Essex, Middlesex, Norfolk, Plymouth and Suffolk counties.
